what_helped: Searching the literal tweet claim ('Italian deli owner confronts ICE') immediately returned fact-check coverage — no need to pre-assume it was fake
The visible AI artifact in the tweet's own media description (officer vest reads 'PICF' not 'ICE') provided a strong targeted query term
Searching for the broader pattern ('AI ICE videos') surfaced multiple authoritative outlets (Boston Globe, Euronews, HuffPost) that independently corroborate the fake nature of this specific video
Comments in the tweet itself (multiple users calling it AI) were a strong prior for query framing
what_hurt: Inquisitr article (most directly relevant) returned 403 and could not be fetched; MSN mirror also failed to return content
No dedicated Snopes or Lead Stories article specifically on the deli video was found — Snopes covers the category but not this exact video
Robin Monotti's name as the poster did not add signal — the video predates his tweet and was shared widely before he posted it
insights.would_multipass_help: no — Round 1 queries surfaced the key sources. The core verdict (AI-generated video) was established immediately from the plain-claim search. Additional passes only confirmed details already found.
insights.deepseek_advice: For tweets posting a dramatic video clip as if real, first search the literal claim as stated, then add 'AI generated' or 'fake' as a second query variant. Look for telltale AI artifacts mentioned in the media description (misspelled text like 'PICF' instead of 'ICE', unnatural props). When multiple reply comments call it AI, weight that heavily as a prior and include 'AI' or 'deepfake' in at least one query.
